note: PHASE 11.1 -- RECOVERY of PR #138, which was never merged and never abandoned: it was AUTO-CLOSED by GitHub when its base branch ci/honest-checks was deleted after #136 landed as a squash. The stacked-squash gotcha, recorded in the 2026-08-04 handover. The commit 68dd2bd survived on origin the whole time; nothing was lost, but nothing was on main either, and `skipIfWalledPreview` is absent from main to this day. DELIVERABLE: one skipIfWalledPreview() helper in scripts/lib/previewProbe.mjs collapsing the near-duplicate preview-wall skip blocks in check-og-images.mjs and check-seo.mjs, with the isPreviewHost gate moved INSIDE the helper. That gate placement is the whole point: with it outside, every caller had to remember it, and a caller that forgot would green-skip a PRODUCTION base on a proven wall -- a silent skip of the real thing. Inside, a non-preview base returns false by construction and the check runs. A timeout, DNS death or broken preview is still NOT a wall, so those fall through and fail loud rather than skipping green. HONEST SCOPE recorded in the docblock: the shared annotation says 'Production is still covered by the scheduled run', which is TRUE only for checks that HAVE a cron run (og-check, seo-check). A check with no scheduled production run -- lighthouse, whose perf-budget.yml is PR/push-only -- must NOT use this helper's wording and keeps its own annotation. RATCHET -- AND THE REVIEW FINDING THAT REVERSED IT, the sharpest of the whole arc. The first cut of this ship re-baselined the allowlist 104 -> 102, dropping the R1:walled-preview rows for check-og-images.mjs and check-seo.mjs, and the ratchet's stale-entry check ENDORSED it by naming both rows as fixed. It was a FALSE win. R1's trigger is a source regex, /previewIsWalled\s*\(/, and `skipIfWalledPreview` does not contain that substring -- capital IsW against Is-W. The call sites moved from previewIsWalled() to the wrapper and the skip construct did not change by one character; the rule simply went blind. Proven by re-running findSilentSkips over the shipped sources with the identifier renamed back: 0 hits as shipped, 1 hit each at check-og-images.mjs:210 and check-seo.mjs:221 when renamed. The meta-guard -- the one this arc built to catch guards that report green without measuring -- was itself reporting green without measuring, and the allowlist delta was recording a debt as PAID that was still owed in full. It would also have become a general escape hatch: any later check adopting the wrapper inherits an R1 exemption nobody reviewed. FOLDED: the trigger now matches BOTH spellings, a self-test case asserts the wrapper form still trips R1 (26 cases, up from 25), and the allowlist is restored to the truthful 104. A mutation narrowing the trigger back reds the new case AND makes the ratchet declare both rows stale -- i.e. it reproduces the false win exactly, which is the proof the fix is real. THE RULE THIS EARNS, and it belongs beside the two already banked: A RATCHET THAT SHRINKS IS NOT SELF-EVIDENTLY A WIN. A row leaving an allowlist means the rule stopped firing, and 'the code was fixed' and 'the rule went blind' are indistinguishable from the count alone. Before banking a shrink, prove the construct is gone -- not merely that the matcher no longer sees it. Corollary: a rule keyed on an IDENTIFIER is only as durable as that name, so every wrapper needs its own case and a self-test beside it. RECOVERY MECHANICS worth keeping: the original branch could not simply be re-targeted at main, because it carries #136's commit b3353d1 underneath and #136 is already on main as a SQUASH, so a PR from it would show a messy re-application. It was instead brought current by merging origin/main in, with .claude/arc-state.json resolved to MAIN's copy -- this ship is a recovery, not an arc phase, so main's phase 11 arc-close record wins and this entry only re-scopes.
